Fixed #37491 -- Reraised RecursionError as ValueError for deeply nested GeoJSON.

json.loads() raises RecursionError rather than JSONDecodeError when the
input nesting exceeds the interpreter's recursion limit. Reraising as
ValueError allows form fields to reraise as ValidationError.

Applying a transform to an annotation alias in values() crashed with
AttributeError when the annotation's output_field was not attached to a
model:

    Book.objects.annotate(published=TruncMonth("pubdate")).values("published__year")

    AttributeError: 'DateField' object has no attribute 'model'

Fixed #36022 -- Renamed django-admin to django.

This change implements DEP 16: to rename the django-admin command to django.
django-admin is kept as an alias.

Docs references to the "django-admin" command are updated to "django" or
“The django command”.

Renamed the `django-admin` Sphinx directive to `cmd`, and the
`django-admin-option` directive to `cli-option`.

Fixed #20551 -- Renamed duplicate "initial" fixtures in gis_tests.

The distapp, geoapp, geogapp, and relatedapp test apps each shipped a
fixture named "initial". Since loaddata loads every match found in
different fixture directories, each test case using fixtures=["initial"]

commit.message: Added reporter's right of first refusal to contributing docs.
Refs #37371 -- Added test databases to .gitignore.

Fixed #37469 -- Made psycopg adapter UTF8Dumper handle None.

The adapter for psycopg2 serialized None to SQL NULL [1]. This behavior
should be maintained for psycopg3, as psql_escape returns None when no
value remain after escaping and stripping.

Thanks to Camille Daniel for the initial bug report.

[1] https://github.com/psycopg/psycopg2/blob/7d0375492ec3707b82b89f632c9654b400466d86/psycopg/adapter_asis.c#L42-L45
Added requirement for a single vulnerability per email.
Added stub release notes for 6.1.4.

Fixed CVE-2026-114582 -- Blocked file and network access when setting SRS on GDAL 3.9+.

Anything instantating `SpatialReference`, including vector and raster
`transform()` methods and `srs`/`srid` setters, was subject to request
forgery from untrusted strings, since GDAL resolves file and network
references by default.

On GDAL 3.9+, Django now uses `OSRSetFromUserInputEx()` to block file
and network access in this path. On lower GDAL versions, users should
compare inputs to an allow list or use integers when setting or
transforming a spatial reference system (SRS). A new `gis.W001` check
warns if a lower GDAL version is installed.

Thanks Adraca for the report and Sarah Boyce and David Smith for reviews.

Fixed CVE-2026-113733 -- Fixed password hash disclosure to "view only" admin users with custom user models.

Since Django 6.0, the admin obfuscated the password hash only when the
field's model was exactly AUTH_USER_MODEL. Other user models, and user
models inheriting the password field from a concrete parent model,
failed that check, so the full hash was displayed to users with only
the view permission.

Thanks to Aaron chen for the report, and Jake Howard for the review.

Fixed CVE-2026-113593 -- Differentiated empty and missing headers in response cache.

When learning the cache key for a response, a missing header must be
cached differently to an empty one, as per RFC 9111.

Thanks to Andrew Gonzalez for the report.

Co-authored-by: Jake Howard <git@theorangeone.net>

Fixed CVE-2026-111362 -- Blocked external CRS values in GeoJSON geometries.

Even though the "crs" member was removed from the GeoJSON spec in 2016,
GDAL's GeoJSON parser still supports this value and can resolve file and
network locations. An attacker could submit a malicious CRS that would
make a network request as the Django process user, or read a file, or
both. Django now rejects these values when constructing geometries and
in forms and lookups. (Utilities for processing trusted data such as
`DataSource` and `LayerMapping` continue to forward these values to GDAL
without validation.)

Any `crs` definition with `"type": "link"` or `"type": "url"` is now
rejected outright. Any definition with `"type": "name"` has its
`properties.name` compared to an allow list of known authorities, or a
regex for an OGC CRS URN, or well-known shorthands, e.g. "CRS84".

Thanks to Submersion Security Research Team for the report, and David
Smith and Sarah Boyce for the reviews.

Fixed CVE-2026-111211 -- Escaped log messages in BaseGeometryWidget.deserialize().

Suitably crafted values submitted to a GeometryField may have allowed
log injection, potentially corrupting log files, obscuring other
attacks, misleading log post-processing tools, or forging log entries.

To mitigate this, invalid values logged on deserialization errors are
now escaped using "unicode_escape" encoding, and trimmed to 4096
characters to avoid flooding logs with large inputs.

Thanks to Aaron chen for the report, and to Jacob Walls, Jake Howard,
and Shai Berger for the reviews.

Co-authored-by: Natalia <124304+nessita@users.noreply.github.com>

Fixed CVE-2026-108147 -- Bounded memory use of base64 file uploads in MultiPartParser.

The mitigation for CVE-2026-33033 aligned base64 data to a multiple of
4 by reading whole chunks. As the chunk size is itself a multiple of 4,
those reads never restored the alignment, so a misaligned upload was
read and decoded in full before reaching upload handlers.

Trailing undecoded bytes are now carried over to the next chunk, so no
extra reads are needed and memory use stays bounded by the chunk size.

Thanks to Ignacy Kujawa for the report, and Jake Howard for the review.
Fixed #37468 -- Clarified the effects of changing primary keys to existing values.

Fixed #37436 -- Avoided overwriting when FETCH_PEERS fetches deferred fields.

If a deferred field has been plucked via `refresh_from_db(fields=...)`
or modified by assigning an attribute, it shouldn't be overwritten when
attribute access on a peer triggers a `fetch_many()`.

The peer fetching should also tolerate deleted instances.

Co-authored-by: Vishy <vishyzero@gmail.com>
Fixed #37467 -- Fixed deletion of cookies with __Http- and __Host-Http- prefixes.
Refs #35514, #37293 -- Corrected removal version for EMAIL_* settings in 6.1 release notes.

Fixed #37138 -- Changed docs to use customized pydata-sphinx-theme.

Updated custom djangodocs Sphinx theme to switch to pydata-sphinx-theme
(PST) with minimal customizations:
* Replaced PST's split top/left main nav with single left sidebar main
  nav. (Borrowed approach from sphinx-book-theme.)
* Moved `docstitle` from navbar_start (in "logo") to navbar_center, to
  avoid wrapping in the header with long development version numbers.

Thanks to Natalia Bidart for review and improvements.

Refs #37271, #37272 -- Doc'd remaining DEP 20 changes for users and releasers.

Starting with Django 2028, DEP 20 changes the Python version support
policy, gives every feature release three years of support, and moves
to calendar versions. Documented these in the Python version FAQ, the
upgrade guide, and the release how-to.

Fixed `make.bat check` to exit non-zero when a check fails.

The target called the lint, black, and spelling subroutines in sequence
and then exited with the status of the last one, so a failure in an
earlier check was printed to the screen but still reported overall
success. It now records each failure and exits non-zero if any check
failed, matching the equivalent `Makefile` target.

Spelling is also run with `-q -W` under `check`, as the `Makefile` does.

Ran docs checks and sphinx_tests on Windows via GitHub Actions.

Created a docs_win.yml workflow paralleling docs.yml but on Windows, to
verify the make.bat checks work like their Makefile counterparts.

Used a separate workflow to limit runs to changes that might affect docs
tooling on Windows.

Spelling is not checked on Windows. PyEnchant resolves en_US from the
hunspell dictionary bundled in its own wheel rather than from a system
dictionary, so a Windows run would enforce a different word list than
the one used on Ubuntu.

Thanks to Natalia Bidart for review and improvements.

Refs #35874 -- Excluded console-tabs.css from epub building on Windows.

Updated fix from commit 8274ae1 to build the path with `os.path.join()`.
Sphinx matches `epub_exclude_files` against OS native paths, so the
hardcoded forward slash never matched on Windows.

Ensured docs checks cover same files as docs builds.

Updated docs `make black` and `make lint` checks to use Sphinx's own
source file discovery to get the list of docs source files. This makes
docs/conf.py the single source of truth for which files are/aren't docs
sources. The exclusions were previously duplicated by hand in Makefile,
make.bat, and lint.py, where they could drift from conf.py.

Created a Python blacken-sources.py wrapper around blacken-docs, similar
to the existing lint.py for sphinx-lint. This replaces shell and batch
file commands that tried (only partially successfully) to replicate
Sphinx's source discovery.

Removed `--jobs 0` from the sphinx-lint arguments to allow parallel
linting, since sphinx-lint treats `--jobs 0` as serial instead of
defaulting to `auto`.

Also added Sphinx to the tox environments running the docs checks, since
neither `blacken-docs` nor `sphinx-lint` depends on Sphinx.

Thanks to Natalia Bidart for review and improvements.

Refs #35874 -- Fixed console tabs overflow in narrow windows.

Fixed a problem introduced in 0e128d5 where wide console content could
appear flush right in narrow windows, clipped off the left side
(depending on the theme). Constrained the tab content <section> to the
available width with horizontal scrolling by default. This also works
correctly with themes that wrap overflow text in Pygments code blocks
(e.g., djangoproject.com).

Refs #35874 -- Excluded console-tabs.css from epub.

Fixed epubcheck validation failures related to console-tabs.css modern
CSS syntax by preventing it from being bundled into epub output. (Since
console tabs are not rendered for epub, the css isn't needed.)

Fixed #37456 -- Converted contribution process diagram to plain SVG.

The draw.io export used HTML labels inside `foreignObject` elements,
including a `<font>` element, which made the epub build fail EPUBCheck
validation. It also embedded about 20KB of draw.io source, and its
light-dark() colors could not be edited in SVG editors like Inkscape.

Labels are now SVG text elements, light colors are presentation
attributes, and dark mode is a prefers-color-scheme media query. In
dark mode, arrows keep the color of the role making each transition,
matching the legend.

Thanks Mike Edmunds for the report.

Regression in eaf7b563a5d3861026242fdb503a58f71acf17f6.
Confirmed release date for 6.1.3, 6.0.10, and 5.2.19.
Fixed #35225 -- Skipped JSONObject ordering tests on Oracle 21c.
Fixed #37432 -- Made select_for_update() raise after combined queries.

Fixed #37438 -- Fixed join promotion for XOR conditions.

JoinPromoter didn't handle XOR conditions. Because of this, a negated
XOR could use an INNER JOIN and remove rows that should be returned.

Thanks Simon Charette and Sarah Boyce for review.
Fixed #37370 -- Reorganized the security policy page.

Fixed #37232 -- Added support for the HTTP QUERY method.

QUERY (RFC 10008) is a safe, idempotent method that carries the query in
the request content rather than in the URI's query component. Treat it as
safe throughout: exempt it from CSRF protection, evaluate request
preconditions as for GET, accept it in require_safe(), and dispatch it
from View. Query content is available as HttpRequest.body and is not
parsed into HttpRequest.POST.

Caching is left for a follow-up. Per RFC 10008 Section 2.7 the cache key
for a QUERY request must incorporate the request content, which the cache
middleware and cache_page() don't do, so they continue to ignore QUERY.

Thanks Ben Atkinson, Jonathan Biemond, and Jacob Walls for reviews.

Fixed #37450 -- Fixed parsing of comment and verbatim tags without spaces.

Regression in 1a9fba7a6c2a0acead19bbb45c25ceb0fdcca7c8.

Fixed #37427 -- Kept generic relation queryset routing lazy.

Generic relation managers eagerly bound querysets to a read database,
causing implicit subqueries to fail when the outer query used another
connection.

Passed the related instance as a routing hint while preserving explicit
database choices, and added a regression test for the reported case.

Thank you to Simon Charette for the review.

Refs #36664 -- Fixed python version labels in GeoDjango CI workflow.

The Postgres 17 jobs were intentionally left on Python 3.14.

Follow-up to c6ebf51871fa149e88f39ea44aaf700590366607.

Refs #35874 -- Improved documentation console tabs accessibility.

Improved accessibility for docs console tabs within constraints of the
current CSS-only, hidden radio button implementation.

* Switched to flex layout. (Previous `text-align: right` could cause
  problems in rtl scripts.)

* Changed radio buttons from `display: none` to visually hidden. This
  allows them to participate in keyboard navigation (with or without
  a screen reader).

* Rendered a focus outline on the visible label when the hidden radio
  button has focus.

* Increased border widths on the active tab to allow distinguishing it
  with high contrast settings (forced-colors: active).

* Increased contrast on inactive tab label and active tab border.

* Created `--tab-*` CSS properties in `.console-block` to allow adapting
  to other themes or contexts (e.g., on docs.djangoproject.com).

Screen readers will announce console tabs as radio buttons. (JavaScript
would be needed to properly implement the WAI-ARIA tab pattern with the
expected behavior for tab-group, tab, and tab-panel ARIA roles.)

Thanks to Natalia Bidart (nessita), Tom Carrick, and Akintola Rahmat for
their reviews and suggestions.
Updated asgiref dependency.

Fixed #30949 -- Deprecated django.utils.functional.cached_property.

Co-authored-by: Natalia <124304+nessita@users.noreply.github.com>

Refs #30949 -- Replaced django.utils.functional.cached_property with functools.cached_property.

Since Python 3.12, `functools.cached_property` no longer takes a lock
(https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/87634), which was the main
objection to using it instead of Django's own implementation.

`Prefetch(to_attr=...)` and the admindocs model detail page now accept
`functools.cached_property` as well as Django's own `cached_property`.

Co-authored-by: Natalia <124304+nessita@users.noreply.github.com>
Fixed #37449 -- Corrected local name for Punjabi in django/conf/locale/__init__.py.

Fixed test_asgeojson() on MySQL 9.5.

MySQL 9.5 added support for the "crs" attribute in GeoJSON:
https://dev.mysql.com/doc/relnotes/mysql/9.7/en/news-9-5-0.html#:~:text=ST_AsGeoJSON%20function

Refs #36664 -- Installed gettext in scheduled Windows tests.

Without `xgettext`, the extraction tests were skipped on the scheduled
Windows jobs, so failures such as #37447 went unnoticed. Also simplified
the gettext installation step in both workflows.

Fixed #37447 -- Fixed makemessages with non-ASCII file names on Windows.

Python 3.15 enables UTF-8 mode by default, so the temporary file
listing the files to process was written as UTF-8. xgettext opens
these paths as raw bytes, which Windows interprets in the ANSI code
page, so non-ASCII file names could not be found.

Refs #36664.

Fixed #37395 -- Emitted 'none' for CSP directives left empty by an unused nonce.

Before, if a directive's only source was a nonce, and that nonce was not rendered,
the directive was omitted, when in reality we should consider the set of scripts
matching the nonce to be empty, and instead fail closed.

Thanks Rob Hudson for the implementation idea and review.

Fixed #37401 -- Aligned safe_makedirs() with os.makedirs() semantics.

Python 3.15 added the `parent_mode` argument to `os.makedirs()`, the
upstream fix for the issue that led Django to vendor its own
`makedirs()` in the fix for CVE-2026-25674. The vendored copy differed
from CPython only by an extra `chmod()` call that ignored the process
umask. Dropping that call allows using `os.makedirs()` directly on
Python 3.15+, and removing the vendored copy once Python 3.14 support
ends.

As a trade-off, directories created by `FileSystemStorage` when
`FILE_UPLOAD_DIRECTORY_PERMISSIONS` (or `directory_permissions_mode`) is
set, and by `FileBasedCache`, now have the requested permissions mode
combined with the process umask, and the set-group-ID bit and other
bits beyond the last 9 are no longer guaranteed to be set.
`FILE_UPLOAD_PERMISSIONS` is unaffected.

Thanks Shai Berger for the proposal and review, Ken Whitesell and
Carlton Gibson for the discussion, and Tim Schilling, Jacob Walls, and
Lily for reviews.

Refs #36664.
Documented the "Low" ticket severity in triaging docs.

Fixed #37433 -- Escaped database error messages logged by Q.check().

Database error messages can include the values being validated, which
may originate from user input. Logging them through `log_message()`
escapes their content and keeps large values trimmed, consistent with
other logging call sites.

Thanks Jacob Walls for reviews.

Refs #37433 -- Added django.utils.text.trim_value() helper.

The debug page and the raster lookup check each trimmed large values
to 4096 characters with their own copy of the same code. The shared
helper also corrects the suffix, which reported characters as bytes
and showed the original length as if it were the amount trimmed.

The trimmed value and the suffix are returned separately so callers
can escape the value without escaping the suffix.

Refs #34746.
Refs #36717 -- Noted RedirectURLMixin signature changes in 6.1 release notes.

Refs #34865 -- Cleared gc.garbage in test_release_memory_without_garbage_collection().

gc.collect() doesn't actually clear gc.garbage.

Fixed #37396 -- Added gettext to PATH in Windows CI.

Chocolatey's gettext bin directory wasn't on PATH for later steps, so
tests requiring msgfmt and xgettext were skipped on Windows.

Skipped PoFileTests.test_no_write_access on Windows, where chmod()
cannot make a directory read-only.

Fixed #37419 -- Included CSP nonces in headers for streaming responses.

Thank you Michael Codispoti (codispoti) for the report. Thank you to
Jake Howard, Jacob Walls and Rob Hudson for the reviews.
Refs #37419 -- Moved CSP nonce detection helper to django.utils.csp for middleware reuse.
Fixed #37407 -- Prevented UUIDTextMixin from mutating the lookup in-place.
Fixed #37431 -- Added support for serializing frozendicts in migrations.

Doc'd ContentType.model_class behaviour for stale content types.

ba7206cd8 (for Django 1.7) made the return type of
ContentType.model_class optional, in the case of stale content types
(essentially for deleted models). Previously this would raise
`LookupError`.

It's a niche case but, the behaviour here was undocumented, requiring
a trip to the source code to determine. This change adds a small note
to the bottom of the docs section, and tweaks the method docstring to
clarify that the return type is optional.
Fixed #37426 -- Added a pull request limit for new contributors.
Refs #37426 -- Moved scripts GitHub API helpers to a shared module for reuse.
Fixed #36664 -- Doc'd Python 3.15 compatibility.
